title: Japan Ke 3 Paise Wale Tarike
note:
METHOD FOUR — TARU WO SHIRU, the hard one. The s72->s73 shove that
     announces it lives on the concat boundary; inside this project s73 is
     simply the first frame.

     Ground arc: amber on the promise break -> neutral through Ryoan-ji ->
     amber on the design -> cool as it comes apart -> warm on your own list ->
     red on the line that moved -> neutral on what happened -> the chapter's
     hottest red on the market that runs on it -> green on the question and on
     writing it down -> neutral out.

     Archetypes: A A A D D D A B A A A A. D is held across s76/s77 because they
     are a matched-frame hold on one photograph AND one continuous diagram: the
     four glyphs share a square in s76, and in s77 the square goes and they come
     apart. That is the only place in the cut where a drawn layer survives a
     scene boundary, and it is what "none of them stands alone" means.

     s79 was proposed with a moving line and cut: the photograph is already a
     chalk line half rubbed out, so a drawn moving line would trace it.

s73.comment:
7.1 · A · PLATE · target · amber — THERE IS A FOURTH. A mossy path in mist;
     the promise break is carried by the line.

s74.comment: 7.2 · A · PLATE · no role · neutral — RYOAN-JI. Raked gravel.

s75.comment:
7.3 · A · PLATE · no role · warm — WHAT IT SAYS. The tsukubai from above,
     with the inscription cited underneath.

s76.comment:
7.4 · D · BAND · target · amber — THE DESIGN. A macro of the basin shows the
     square opening; it cannot show that four separate characters each use it.
     Four blocks around one shared square — the claim, drawn.
